newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf forges ahead with asset sale programme.
newsitem.headline: Elf forges ahead with asset sale programme.

text.p: French oil group Elf Aquitaine forged ahead with its asset disposal programme and said on Friday it had placed a 10 percent stake in engineering company Geophysique.

The placement of 400,000 shares, which market sources said was executed at 365 francs for a total amount of 146 million francs, reduced the oil group's stake in Compagnie Generale de Geophysique (CGG) to 11 percent.
The Geophysique placement is the latest in a series of operations carried out as part of Elf Aquitaine chairman Phillipe Jaffre's two-year asset sale and debt reduction programme.
Earlier this month, it signed a joint venture agreement with Chevron Corp subsidiary Gulf Oil and Murphy Petroleum which would save 50 million pounds per year.

In October, Elf sold its 2.9 percent stake in Cie Financiere de Suez to Belgium's Electrafina for six billion Belgian francs and a 7.06 percent stake in Belgium's Compagnie Nationale a Portefeuille (CNP) to Fibelpar.
In May, Elf sold a one percent stake in Generale des Eaux and in January it placed a 12.9 percent stake in Enterprise Oil Plc.
Jaffre said in February that the group had sold 15 billion francs of assets in 1995 and added at the time that there was still some 1.5 billion francs in assets left to sell when the price was right.
The sale programme is part of Jaffre's campaign to have a return on equity of at least 10 percent in 1998, against seven percent in 1995.
The debt to equity ratio stood at 38 percent at the end-year, down from 46 percent.
Elf shares gained 1.71 percent to 457.90 francs on Friday while the blue-chip index was up 0.98 percent but analysts said this was not totally due to the latest asset sale.
One French broker said there was some arbitrage between the oil majors, with Elf benefiting from a premium of around 40 francs over Total, the widest spread seen for some time.
Some operators were buying Elf and selling Total, which pushed out the share price spread between the two stocks, the broker said.
Oils have risen with the firming in world crude prices.
Elf was further bolstered by last week's sale of a nine percent stake by the French government which eliminated a stock overhang which had depressed the share for a long time.
